아홉.forms: native · counting things, hours, age · same before a counter (아홉 개, 아홉 시)
아홉.e: Hours use native numbers: 아홉 시 = 9 o'clock.

감정.ex: 그는 자기 감정을 잘 표현하지 않아요.
감정.x: He doesn't really express his feelings.
감정.t: 기분 is your mood right now; 감정 is the general word for emotions.

감정.ex: 할머니가 물려주신 도자기의 감정을 받아 봤어요.
감정.x: I had the pottery my grandmother left me appraised.
감정.t: Different from 감정 'emotion' (感情); appraisal usually appears as 감정을 받다 or 감정을 의뢰하다.

단풍.ex: 가을에 설악산에 가면 단풍이 정말 예뻐요.
단풍.x: If you go to Seoraksan in the fall, the autumn leaves are really beautiful.
단풍.e: Literally 'red maple'; now it means any leaves turning color.

외식.x: On weekends, I often eat out with my family.
외식.t: Add 하다 to make the verb: 외식하다 'to eat out'.

만족.ex: 저희 회사는 고객의 만족을 가장 중요하게 생각합니다.
만족.x: Our company considers customer satisfaction the most important thing.

인생.x: The most important thing in life is health.
인생.t: 인생 is life as a whole journey; 생활 is day-to-day living; 생명 is biological life.

참석.ex: 회의 참석 여부를 오늘까지 알려 주세요.
참석.x: Please let us know by today whether you'll attend the meeting.
참석.e: Literally 'join a seat' — take your seat at an event.
참석.t: 참석 is attending (a meeting, a wedding); 참가 is actively taking part (a contest).

대책.m: countermeasure, measure, plan to deal with something
대책.ex: 정부는 미세먼지 대책을 빨리 세워야 합니다.
대책.x: The government needs to come up with measures against fine dust quickly.
대책.e: Literally 'a plan for facing' a problem.
대책.t: The usual verb is 세우다: 대책을 세우다, 'to come up with measures.'

곤충.ex: 여름에는 숲에서 다양한 곤충을 볼 수 있어요.
곤충.x: In summer you can see all kinds of insects in the forest.
곤충.e: The scientific word for insect; everyday 'bug' is 벌레.

인식.ex: 환경 문제에 대한 사람들의 인식이 바뀌고 있어요.
인식.x: People's awareness of environmental issues is changing.
인식.t: Very common in reading passages as N에 대한 인식 'perception of N'.

하락.ex: 주가 하락 때문에 걱정하는 사람이 많습니다.
하락.x: Many people are worried because of the drop in stock prices.

거리 공연.ex: 주말이면 공원에서 거리 공연이 자주 열려요.
거리 공연.x: On weekends there are often street performances in the park.
거리 공연.t: Common in news and on signs; in casual talk people often say 버스킹. A performance is held is 공연이 열리다.

시각.ex: 같은 일도 시각에 따라 다르게 보일 수 있어요.
시각.x: The same thing can look different depending on your point of view.
시각.e: Literally 'viewing angle'; a homonym 시각 means 'time, moment'.

단속.ex: 오늘 밤 이 도로에서 음주 운전 단속이 있어요.
단속.x: There is a drunk-driving checkpoint on this road tonight.
단속.e: Literally 'gather and bind'—keeping things tightly under control.
단속.t: 단속에 걸리다 'to get caught in a crackdown' is very common.

가뜩이나.m: as it is, already (and on top of that)
가뜩이나.x: I'm busy as it is, and now my computer's broken too.
가뜩이나.e: Probably related to 가득 'full' — already full of trouble.
가뜩이나.t: Almost always followed by -(으)ㄴ데/-는데 and then a complaint.

지극히.forms: 지극히 + adjective: 지극히 정상적이다, 지극히 개인적인
지극히.x: That's just my very personal opinion.
지극히.t: Pronounced [지그키] — ㄱ and ㅎ merge into ㅋ.

턱없이.forms: 턱없이 + adjective: 턱없이 부족하다, 턱없이 비싸다
턱없이.ex: 이 돈으로는 여행 경비가 턱없이 부족해요.
턱없이.x: This money falls far short of what the trip costs.
턱없이.e: 턱 here means 'grounds, reason' (not the chin): 'without reason'.
턱없이.t: Pronounced [터겁씨]; 턱없이 부족하다 'woefully insufficient' is the top collocation.

발상.ex: 발상을 바꾸면 문제가 쉽게 풀릴 수 있어요.
발상.x: If you change your way of thinking, the problem may be easy to solve.
발상.t: Pronounced [발쌍]; 발상의 전환 (a shift in thinking) is a common set phrase.

사명감.m: sense of duty, sense of mission
사명감.ex: 그 의사는 강한 사명감을 가지고 일해요.
사명감.x: That doctor works with a strong sense of mission.

시댁.m: husband's family, in-laws' home (from the wife's view)
시댁.ex: 이번 추석에는 시댁에 먼저 가기로 했어요.
시댁.x: This Chuseok, we decided to visit my husband's family first.
시댁.e: 시- marks the husband's side: 시어머니, 시아버지; -댁 is the polite word for 'house.'
시댁.t: Only a wife says 시댁; a husband calls his wife's family 처가.

부업.m: side job, side business, side hustle
부업.x: My salary alone isn't enough, so I started a side job.
부업.t: 투잡 'two jobs' is a casual equivalent, and N잡러 is slang for someone juggling several jobs.

발탁.x: He was picked as a minister at a young age.
발탁.t: Often passive: N(으)로 발탁되다 = to be picked as N.

멸망.x: Unified Silla fell in 935 when it surrendered to Goryeo.

선동하다.m: to incite, to stir up, to agitate
선동하다.x: He stirred people up with false information.
선동하다.e: Literally 'fan and move' — fanning the flames of emotion.

재평가하다.ex: 역사학자들은 그 왕의 업적을 재평가하고 있어요.
재평가하다.x: Historians are reassessing that king's achievements.
재평가하다.e: Literally 'judge the value again'; 재- = re-: 재평가, 재구성, 재편.

굳히다.m: to harden, to set; to solidify, to firm up (a decision, position)
굳히다.ex: 그는 오랜 고민 끝에 유학을 가기로 마음을 굳혔어요.
굳히다.x: After much thought, he made up his mind to study abroad.
굳히다.t: Pronounced [구치다] — palatalization. Collocations: 마음을 굳히다, 입지를 굳히다, 1위를 굳히다.

이윽고.forms: Literary; casual equivalent: 잠시 후, 얼마 후
이윽고.m: after a while, presently, before long
이윽고.ex: 기차가 천천히 멈추고 이윽고 문이 열렸어요.
이윽고.x: The train slowly stopped, and before long the doors opened.
이윽고.e: A literary word, common in novels and fairy tales rather than conversation.

격의 없이.forms: 격의 없이 대화하다 · 격의 없는 + noun
격의 없이.ex: 사장님과 직원들이 격의 없이 이야기를 나눴어요.
격의 없이.x: The boss and the employees chatted openly, without formality.
격의 없이.e: Literally 'without a separating mind' — no emotional barrier between people.

일장일단.m: pros and cons, strengths and weaknesses
일장일단.x: Both methods have their pros and cons.
일장일단.e: Literally 'one long point, one short point' — one strength, one weakness.
일장일단.t: Almost always in 일장일단이 있다 'each has its pros and cons'.

불을 보듯 뻔하다.forms: 불을 보듯 뻔해요 · 불을 보듯 뻔했어요 · 불 보듯 뻔한 + noun
불을 보듯 뻔하다.m: to be obvious; to be as plain as day
불을 보듯 뻔하다.ex: 준비를 안 하면 결과는 불을 보듯 뻔해요.
불을 보듯 뻔하다.x: If you don't prepare, the result is as plain as day.
불을 보듯 뻔하다.e: Literally 'as obvious as looking at a fire.'

일제 강점기.ex: 일제 강점기에 많은 사람들이 독립운동을 했습니다.
일제 강점기.x: During the Japanese colonial period, many people took part in the independence movement.
일제 강점기.e: Literally 'period of forced occupation by imperial Japan'.
일제 강점기.t: Koreans use this term, not 'colonial era', to stress the occupation was forced.

도량.ex: 그는 남의 실수를 웃어넘길 만큼 도량이 넓어요.
도량.x: He's broad-minded enough to laugh off other people's mistakes.
도량.e: Literally 'measure and capacity' — how much your heart can hold.
도량.t: Almost always 도량이 넓다 / 크다 (broad-minded) or 도량이 좁다 (petty).

머리가 굳다.m: to be slow to learn new things, one's mind gets rusty; to become rigid in one's thinking (lit. the head hardens)
머리가 굳다.ex: 나이가 드니까 머리가 굳어서 단어가 잘 안 외워져요.
머리가 굳다.x: Now that I'm older, my brain has gotten rusty and words just don't stick.
머리가 굳다.e: Like clay or cooked rice that hardens over time, the mind loses its flexibility.
머리가 굳다.t: Often said self-deprecatingly about age or a long break from studying: 머리가 굳었나 봐요.

헌법재판소.ex: 헌법재판소는 그 법률이 헌법에 위반된다고 결정했습니다.
헌법재판소.x: The Constitutional Court ruled that the law violates the Constitution.
헌법재판소.t: News usually shortens it to 헌재.

감형.x: On appeal, his sentence was reduced from five years to three.

고정비.ex: 매달 내는 월세와 보험료는 대표적인 고정비입니다.
고정비.x: Monthly rent and insurance are typical fixed costs.
고정비.e: 고정 'fixed' + -비 'cost,' a common suffix: 교통비, 식비.

배타적경제수역.ex: 중국 어선이 우리 배타적경제수역에서 불법 조업을 했습니다.
배타적경제수역.x: Chinese fishing boats fished illegally in our exclusive economic zone.
배타적경제수역.e: Literally 'other-excluding economic water area'; it reaches 200 nautical miles offshore.
배타적경제수역.t: News often just says EEZ, read as 이이지.

비통하다.x: The bereaved families held the funeral with grief-stricken hearts.
비통하다.t: Formal and strong; common in news about deaths and disasters.

변종.ex: 새로운 변종 바이러스가 빠르게 퍼지고 있습니다.
변종.x: A new variant of the virus is spreading quickly.

결핵.ex: 결핵은 기침으로 전염될 수 있는 질병입니다.
결핵.x: Tuberculosis is a disease that can spread through coughing.
결핵.e: Literally 'knotted core' — named for the hard nodules it forms in the lungs.
결핵.t: Doctors often specify 폐결핵 (pulmonary TB), the most common form.

계량.ex: 베이킹을 할 때는 재료 계량이 정말 중요해요.
계량.x: When baking, measuring the ingredients is really important.

선행연구.ex: 논문을 쓰기 전에 선행연구를 꼼꼼히 읽어야 해요.
선행연구.x: Before writing a paper, you should read the previous research carefully.
선행연구.t: Thesis chapters often have a section titled 선행연구 검토 (review of previous studies).

주제의식.m: thematic awareness, a work's sense of purpose
주제의식.ex: 이 영화는 감독의 뚜렷한 주제의식이 돋보여요.
주제의식.x: This film stands out for the director's clear sense of purpose.
주제의식.e: Literally 'theme consciousness' — what the author deliberately wants to say.

삼국시대.ex: 삼국시대에는 고구려, 백제, 신라가 서로 경쟁했어요.
삼국시대.x: During the Three Kingdoms period, Goguryeo, Baekje and Silla competed with each other.
삼국시대.t: Pronounced [삼국씨대] — the ㅅ after ㄱ becomes tense.

금의환향.x: He won a gold medal at the Olympics and returned home in glory.
금의환향.e: Literally 'returning home in silk robes' — coming back a success.
금의환향.t: Usually 금의환향하다; here 금 means 'silk brocade', not 'gold'.

시민의식.x: The audience's civic-mindedness stood out as they took their trash home.
시민의식.t: Korean news often praises or criticizes 시민의식 after big public events.

난립하다.m: to spring up in disorderly numbers, to proliferate
난립하다.x: Ahead of the election, small parties sprang up everywhere.
난립하다.e: Literally 'stand in disorder': too many of something popping up chaotically.
난립하다.t: Pronounced [날리파다] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

제창하다.m: to advocate, to propose, to put forward (an idea or theory)
제창하다.ex: 그 학자는 새로운 경제 이론을 처음 제창했습니다.
제창하다.x: That scholar was the first to propose a new economic theory.
제창하다.e: Literally 'raise and call out' — putting forward a new idea.
제창하다.t: Homonym: 제창 齊唱 means singing in unison, as in 애국가 제창 at ceremonies.

포섭하다.m: to win over, to recruit (to one's side); to subsume
포섭하다.ex: 그들은 내부 직원을 포섭해 정보를 빼냈습니다.
포섭하다.x: They won over an insider and extracted the information.
포섭하다.e: Literally 'wrap and take in' — drawing someone into your group.

일각여삼추.m: a moment feeling like years, waiting impatiently
일각여삼추.ex: 합격 발표를 기다리는 하루가 일각여삼추 같았어요.
일각여삼추.x: Waiting a day for the exam results felt like an eternity.
일각여삼추.e: Literally 'one moment is like three autumns' — i.e. three years.
일각여삼추.t: Usually followed by 같다: 일각여삼추 같다 'every minute feels like years.'
